items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation. The call opened 'This is just with Einstein Moving Company. Com. How can I help you?' and went straight to the record pull. He set a mini-agenda only at the pricing handoff ('I'm ready to get into my estimate for you and the pricing now don't worry about taking notes'), which is 8 minutes too late to frame the call or set a timeframe.
Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up before diving into the quote form.

Save Your Ass section never delivered — 0/10, and the customer teed it up on a platter: 'I have a good two weeks here to get everything cleaned up and boxed up so I'm hopeful that it's a very, very smooth move.' Jespah's answer was 'Yeah overall this is looking like a pretty straightforward one for me as well.' No prep-equals-lower-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close — on a job priced at the 2.5-hour minimum where 30 minutes of prep is real money to the customer.

No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned. The customer raised damage risk himself: 'I have like one picture frame that's a glass... it's a pretty nice picture. So when I've moved that in the past I just like, you know wrap it extra well.' Jespah replied 'Of course. Okay, awesome. I'll make a note about that' — a note instead of the $2,000 coverage pitch.

Insurance explained as generic 'liability coverage' only. The customer then asked a direct insurance question about the building's $1M bonded/COI requirement, and Jespah answered COI logistics well but never explained the No Worries product or the 60c/lb baseline — a second open door on the same subject, missed twice.

On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — notable because the whole back half of the call was about arrival windows ('between 8:30 and nine it's just a thirty minute arrival window'), which is exactly the moment the guarantee lands.

No 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum. He covered clock-starts-on-site and the 2.5-hour minimum, then said only 'you're only charged for the time needed' — the customer never learned how partial hours bill.
No explicit 'no hidden fees' pitch. 'Everything else included' is not the differentiator — no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees was never said.
'No deposit required' never mentioned, on a call where the customer committed to a Saturday date and a specific arrival window.

Email handoff mentioned twice but never specified: no BOLDED key-details framing, no 'reply with any corrections,' and no hours or how-to-reach-us. On a job with two outstanding deliverables (confirmation email plus the COI), verification language mattered more than usual.
No closing 'any other questions before I let you go?' — the customer closed the call himself ('I think I'm all good with that').
Never asked about packing services. The customer said 'I haven't packed it yet' and 'I'll box up all the books,' and packing help was never offered or priced.
Never asked about additional stops, storage stops, or additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony) at either address.
Drive time between origin and destination never mentioned as an estimate variable, even though the estimate hinged on hitting roughly three hours.

Disassembly was named as included ('any tools that we may need for disassemble or reassembly') but never applied to the job — nobody confirmed whether the queen bed, the TV stand, or the bookshelf need to come apart, which is the most likely reason this move runs past the three-hour reservation.
Zip codes not confirmed at either address (street addresses were read back from the quote form).
Customer's name used only twice — 'Is it Jason by chance?' and 'Yeah, Jason. It's my pleasure' — short of the 3+ standard.

Filler and self-interruption throughout: 'what's it called' twice inside the insurance answer, 'Gotcha. Gotcha, okay, awesome,' and a run of restarts ('the, what that includes is obviously'). Also two garbled figures in the transcript — '$222 an hour for 22 guys' (should be a 2-man crew) and 'the three hours comes out to $2,624' (3 x $208 = $624) — see audio review flag.
top_strength: The discovery and estimate work on this call was genuinely good, and it is why a partial online quote turned into a booked Saturday job in 12 minutes. Jespah opened by recapping the record instead of re-interviewing: 'What this is showing, is you're moving from 10909 river plantation drive which is a single story house, moving to 214 Barton springs road, which is a one bedroom apartment, is that right?' — which immediately surfaced the reason the system choked ('the house is two floors but I'm only, I live on the first floor'). He then ran a clean, specific probe: an itemized inventory walk, a specialty-item check ('Would you classify anything there as a specialty item, anything antique or extra heavy'), a box-count anchor using an equivalent ('usually when we're moving the equivalent of roughly just the bedroom's worth of stuff... 1012 boxes or so does that sound roughly right to you?'), a real walk-distance probe ('Do you know like how far the walk is from the elevator to your apartment?'), and an explicit stressor question ('do you have any specific, like, concerns or stressors about the moving process just in general I can address for you?'). He priced all three day tiers unprompted and volunteered the savings — 'If you have flexibility Saturdays are the highest rate of the week. It's variable pricing with us, so if you can do like a Sunday... you can just save up a little bit of money but if it's got to be Saturday that works fine as well' — which is budget-conscious framing without pressure. He built the cushion into the estimate transparently and honestly ('mainly because there's an elevator we gotta go to 13... If it only takes the two and a half that's all you reserved for'), handled the building's $1M COI requirement with confidence and a real turnaround commitment, and then did something above the rubric: he reverse-engineered the customer's freight-elevator reservation off the arrival window ('I think if you start that at about 10:00 that should line up with us'), which is the kind of logistics help that prevents a bad move day.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix is Save Your Ass, and the exact moment is on the transcript. When Jason said 'I have a good two weeks here to get everything cleaned up and boxed up so I'm hopeful that it's a very, very smooth move,' the line Jespah owed him was: 'Jason, that two weeks is the single biggest thing you control on the bill — since you're paying by the hour, every box that's sealed and stacked by the door before we arrive is money back in your pocket. Grab anything loose in drawers, closet odds and ends, the bathroom stuff, and stage it all in one spot. And anything small and fragile — like that glass picture frame — take a carload over yourself the day before if you can. Does that make sense?' On a job reserved at three hours against a 2.5-hour minimum, thirty minutes of prep is roughly $110 to this customer and one less move eating the crew's afternoon — this is the one section with a direct line to estimate accuracy, and it scored zero. Second priority: he was handed the No Worries opening twice — the glass picture frame, then the building's insurance requirement — and both times gave logistics instead of the differentiator. The frame moment needed 'That's exactly what our No Worries Damage Coverage is for — up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage, and I'm noting the frame on the job right now so the crew double-wraps it,' and the COI moment needed the 60c/lb baseline contrast so the customer understood what he actually has. Third, the arrival-window stretch was a free On-Time Guarantee setup: after 'between 8:30 and nine it's just a thirty minute arrival window,' add 'and if we miss that window, we start discounting immediately — that's our On-Time Guarantee.' Two mechanical adds that cost ten seconds each: 'no deposit to hold the date' at the moment he said 'that spot is yours,' and framing the confirmation email as 'the key details are bolded at the top — reply with any corrections.' Business follow-up to verify in EMMA: the COI request to the insurance provider was promised verbally ('I'll send a request to our insurance provider... turnaround time is like a day or so') and the move cannot happen without it clearing the building, so confirm it was actually submitted and logged, along with unit 1320 and the glass-frame note.
phone_presence_notes: Easy, conversational warmth throughout with natural acknowledgments ('Gotcha, okay. Yeah, that makes sense,' 'Of course') and a genuinely warm close ('Yeah, Jason. It's my pleasure. I hope you have a good rest of your day') that left the customer volunteering 'thank you very much I appreciate the help' — held back from a 5 by heavy filler, only two name uses, and no humor or rapport moment.
audio_review_reason: Two pricing figures are garbled in the transcript and need verification against audio: '$222 an hour for 22 guys' (should be a 2-man crew) and 'Monday through Thursday... that's $208 and the three hours comes out to $2,624' (3 x $208 = $624). If the $2,624 was actually spoken, the customer was quoted a weekday total roughly 4x too high on the exact comparison he asked for, which would change his choice of Saturday.
